channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: US Dollar: Jackson Hole scenarios shape FX risk – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny and Abdul-Ahad Lockhart argue that Jackson Hole only becomes a significant FX event for the Dollar when the Federal Reserve Chair delivers a clear policy surprise or commits to future action.

item.title: Canadian Dollar awaits fresh catalyst with Warsh, GDP data in focus
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3845 on Friday, edging 0.07% lower on the day, as investors refrain from taking large positions ahead of the highly anticipated speech by Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole Symposium.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Election polls and carry underpin BRL – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes a supportive backdrop for carry trades and says the Brazilian Real (BRL) is also benefiting from polling that narrows President Lula’s lead over Flavio Bolsonaro to one point.

item.title: “State terrorism”: Iran condemns new US economic measures
item.description: Iran strongly condemned the latest economic measures imposed by the United States (US) on Friday, describing Washington's sanctions policy as “state terrorism”, according to a statement from the Iranian Foreign Ministry cited by Reuters.

item.title: Australian Dollar tests three-month highs above 0.7200 with all eyes on Fed’s Warsh
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) ticks higher for the fourth consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD) as investors brace for the Federal Reserve (Fed) Chairman Kevin Warsh’s speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium, due later on Friday.

item.title: "Anything else would likely put the Japanese Yen under significant pressure": Commerzbank on why BoJ should hike rates
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) is holding within a narrow trading range against the US Dollar (USD) at around 159.35, but pressures are rising following an acceleration in Tokyo inflation data.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade war clouds Q2 GDP rebound – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes USD/CAD is trading just above its 200‑day moving average near 1.3840 as Canada’s Q2 GDP is expected to rebound strongly, with real GDP seen rising 3.4% SAAR versus a slight Q1 contraction.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weak currency and cheap burgers – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Helge J. Pedersen argues that the Japanese Yen appears significantly undervalued versus the Dollar on both OECD purchasing power parity estimates and The Economist’s Big Mac Index.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD hits fresh two-month highs with all eyes on Jackson Hole
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) heads north for the second consecutive day on Friday, with all eyes on the Federal Reserve (Fed) Chairman Kevin Warsh’s speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium, due later on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Bulls challenge 0.7200 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight AUD/USD’s third consecutive daily gain, with the pair stalling just under the 0.7200 resistance.

item.title: Nonfarm Payrolls face a reality check with key benchmark revision
item.description: US investors will watch on Friday a labor market report that is far less familiar than the monthly jobs release but has gained considerable importance following the spectacular revisions of recent years.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $70.41 per troy ounce, up 1.68% from the $69.25 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: British Pound: Energy-driven inflation risks support GBP against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG highlights that rising European natural gas prices are reviving inflation risks, which could push the Bank of England toward another rate hike and underpin the Pound.

item.title: Euro: Options show benefits from US policy doubts – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister reviews EUR/USD options, noting that risk reversals turned positive again after comments by the US Treasury Secretary.

item.title: US Dollar: Warsh speech keeps ranges contained – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes a quiet, risk-positive week for global markets, with low volatility and mixed G10 FX, as the Dollar debasement theme fails to extend.

item.title: Oil: Hormuz stalemate sustains inflation risks - Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen says the US-Iran stalemate and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz are keeping oil-driven inflation risks elevated.

item.title: Swiss Franc consolidates recent losses with the focus turning to Fed’s Warsh
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) trades marginally lower against a somewhat firmer US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with market volatility subdued as investors await the speech of the Federal Reserve (Fed) Chairman, Kevin Warsh, at the Jackson Hole Symposium, due later on the day.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Bearish stance maintained on rate hike pricing – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ FX strategist Howard Du maintains a bearish New Zealand Dollar (NZD) bias, noting that Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) tightening is largely priced and NZD positioning has normalized.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Range trading remains intact against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/JPY held in a narrow band around 159.35, with a slight uptick in upward momentum. They expect this to translate into trading between 159.15 and 159.65 rather than a sustained advance.

item.title: Euro: Focus on Fed signals and Jackson Hole – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note that EUR/USD traded at 1.165 as markets await Fed Chair Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech, which could shift expectations for the September Fed meeting.

item.title: Forex Today: Fed Chair Warsh speech at Jackson Hole, NFP benchmark revision to lift volatility
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Friday, August 28:

item.title: US Dollar: Warsh speech risks asymmetric USD reaction – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes the US Dollar has stabilized after last week’s setback, with Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech seen as the next key test.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Trading sideways around 0.8500 amid fading bullish traction
item.description: The Euro (EUR) nurses moderate losses against the British Pound (GBP), with price action contained within the previous day's range and market volatility muted, as investors brace for Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s speech at Jackson Hole.

item.title: Silver: Consolidation near resistance as positioning builds – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong describes Silver as constructive with room for participation to build, as ETF holdings and managed-money positioning rise from light levels. Technical bias is mildly bullish, but momentum is fading near the 70.60–72 resistance band.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD holds gains above $4,600 as bullish bias prevails
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around $4,610 during the European hours on Friday. The price of the precious metal is remaining within the ascending channel pattern, suggesting a persistent bullish bias.

item.title: Indian Rupee: GDP data to show resilience – DBS
item.description: DBS Group strategists Taimur Baig and Nathan Chow expect India’s 1QFY27 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to confirm that the economy has weathered geopolitical disruptions better than initially feared.

item.title: Asia FX: Central banks act as risk managers – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan reviews recent decisions by Bank of Korea (BoK), Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) and Bank of Japan (BoJ), stressing a shared risk-management approach under uncertainty. BoK and BSP both hiked 25 bps but signalled a slower pace ahead while keeping tightening options open.

item.title: Euro: Range phase caps recent advance against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report EUR/USD held near 1.1650 after a brief dip, with intraday action lacking strong downside momentum.

item.title: Japanese Yen dips further despite hotter inflation, upbeat employment data
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) edges lower for the fifth consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, despite hot Tokyo inflation numbers and an unexpected decline in the Unemployment Rate earlier in the day.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Falls to near $82.00 after breaking below nine-day EMA
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price declines after two days of gains, trading around $82.20 during the European hours on Friday. The technical analysis of the daily chart indicates that the spot is remaining within the ascending channel, suggesting that the primary trend is upward.
